subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class pre-compaction warnings, a structured handoff/checkpoint turn, and bounded deferral authority, and what security/authorization contract should govern them?
rationale: Current main has partial lifecycle hooks, memory flush, notices, and checkpoints, but the requested public config and deferral authority cross session-state and security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Full Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Approve a focused design covering thresholds, handoff/checkpoint envelope, deferral max/audit behavior, expired approval handling, and runtime/protocol ownership before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Warnings Only
options.body: Implement only non-authoritative pre-threshold notices on existing notify/hook surfaces and leave handoff and deferral for a later checkpoint/security design.

options.title: Defer New Core Semantics
options.body: Keep current memoryFlush, hooks, notifyUser, and checkpoint APIs until a concrete reproduced failure justifies additional lifecycle control.

recommendation.title: Design Full Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a focused design covering thresholds, handoff/checkpoint envelope, deferral max/audit behavior, expired approval handling, and runtime/protocol ownership before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the existing pre-compaction memory flush and the remaining lifecycle product decision points to this owner candidate.
